draft.title: Vertical translations
card: A translation slides a graph without changing its shape or size. In y = f(x) + c, the number c is added to every y value.
If c is positive, the graph moves up by c units. If c is negative, it moves down by that many units. For example, y = x² + 3 is y = x² moved up 3.
Every point (x, y) on y = f(x) moves to (x, y + c). The x value stays the same.
Worked example: y = x² has its vertex at (0, 0). For y = x² − 2, the vertex moves to (0, −2), which is 2 units down.
draft.remember: Adding c outside f(x) moves every point up c units, or down if c is negative.

a.q: The graph of y = f(x) is moved to y = f(x) − 4. What happens to the graph?
a.why: Subtracting 4 from every y value lowers each point by 4 units, so the graph moves down. Up is wrong because that would need +4. Left and right are wrong because the x values do not change.
a.clue: Look at what happens to each y value.

b.q: The graph of y = x² has its vertex at (0, 0). Where is the vertex of y = x² + 5?
b.why: Adding 5 to every y value moves the graph up 5 units, so the vertex moves from (0, 0) to (0, 5). (0, −5) is tempting but it is a move down, which needs −5. The x value stays 0.
b.clue: Only the y value of each point changes.
